note: Formats with proven demand (owner reset, 2026-10-21). Every plan's `story` is one of these ids for its format, and its `demand` names a reference video. Research adds formats and examples from the nightly demand scan; the improver retires formats our own numbers say don't work. Views as read on the day in `seen`.

formats.name: Rich vs Poor
formats.emotion: envy and identity: which side am I on?
formats.hook: Two characters, the same moment, opposite moves, in the first second: 'Poor person gets a raise. Rich person gets a raise.'
formats.beats: the same situation for both (raise, bonus, car, first salary) -> what the poor one does, number computed -> what the rich one does, number computed -> the gap after N years, the punchline -> last line leads back to the first
titles: Rich vs Poor: what they do with a {raise}
Poor people buy a car. Rich people buy...
Rich vs Poor: your first salary

examples.title: rich vs poor parents buying you a car

formats.name: What the rich know (and don't tell you)
formats.emotion: curiosity and a feeling of being let in on a secret
formats.hook: A rich mentor character says the secret line first: 'Billionaires don't sell their shares. They borrow against them.' The other character: 'Wait, what?'
formats.beats: the secret in one line -> the normal person's way, with its cost computed -> the rich way step by step, figures computed -> why it works (legal, how) -> the twist or limit (who it doesn't work for) -> loop line
titles: How billionaires never pay tax
Why the rich never sell
The loan rich people love and you're scared of

formats.name: The trap
formats.emotion: fear of being cheated, then relief
formats.hook: The shocking number on screen in the first second: 'This ₹2,000 EMI costs you ₹1.4 lakh.' / 'This $0 down car costs $11,000 extra.'
formats.beats: the shock number -> how the trap looks friendly (0% EMI, minimum due, BNPL, free trial) -> how it really takes your money, computed -> who it is built for (the company's side) -> the one move that beats it -> loop line
titles: The middle class EMI trap
